Lines 7 and 10. "Annual System Production Cost" - consists of fuels and variable operation and maintenance costs from Applicant's Procos Computer Production Cost Study using escalated fuel costs.
Line 8. "Total Annual System Cost", 1985 - sum of lines 6 and 7.
Line 11. "Total Annual System Cost", 1990 - sum of lines 6 and 10.
Line 9. Cost Advantage, Bad Creek ($1,000,000) - the amount in millions of dollars by which the total system cost for the proposed project for the year 1985 is less than (or greater than) the six alternatives studied. It is equal to line 8 cost for alternative minus line 8 cost for Bad Creek.
Line 12. Same explanation as for line 9 except 1990 costs are used.
Fixed charges on existing plant are not included in line 6 values because they are equal in all alternative cases and would be eliminated in the subtraction employed to obtain lines 9 and 12.
Because of uncertainties in long-range fuel cost forecasts and the uncertainties involved in forecasting long-range construction schedules, it is not considered meaningful to estimate the life-time present worth of the project. Table 8-2 shows a substantial increase in the cost advantage of Bad Creek Project between 1985 and 1990. This trend can be expected to continue as long as fuel costs escalate and as additional nuclear units are added to the system. In addition, since the Bad Creek Project is a classical energy storage system it is adaptable to changing forms of energy production. It is completely compatible with wind, solar, and tidal-produced power.
